As someone who has taught plenty of writing intensive mathematics courses to non-STEM majors, I can wholeheartedly agree that flipping the script on the standard methods of assessment can work wonders in the classroom. Such alterations have allowed my non-stem students to develop a deeper appreciation for advanced mathematics overall, to clearly see how creativity plays a vital role in the sciences, and how sandboxing can lead to interesting and profound discoveries in related fields.

However, I believe it's a more laborious procedure to alter methods of assessments for more fast-paced traditional STEM-track courses such as Precalculus and algebra, for example. I would be curious to hear how STEM instructors have "flipped the script" along with any supporting data.

Overall, I really enjoyed the session! Certainly a lot of food for thought! Thank you!
